concerns.text: FR-004 runs 'the identical detection-and-cross-correlation pipeline on each (using the real galaxy mask)' — i.e. only the CMB realization varies while the observed galaxy density field is held fixed. The null distribution then omits galaxy-field (shape-noise, cosmic-variance-of-voids) variance, which is a dominant term in CMB×LSS cross-correlations. This biases the null too narrow and inflates significance. The realizations must also randomize/simulate the galaxy field (or an analytic covariance must be justified).

The sensitivity sweep (7 thresholds × 5 radii = 35 correlated tests) reports raw p-values with no multiple-testing treatment. The Assumptions section claims the 'global Monte-Carlo rank test' addresses multiplicity across redshift bins, but says nothing about the threshold/radius grid. Reporting uncorrected p-values across 35 combinations invites inflated Type-I error; specify a correction or designate one pre-registered baseline configuration with the sweep as descriptive-only.

FR-012 calls Granett et al. 2008 a 'linear-theory model' reference. Granett et al. 2008 is an empirical stacked-void ISW measurement whose amplitude is famously ~2–5× the linear-ΛCDM prediction — it is not a theoretical curve. Using it as the theoretical reference for SC-004 mislabels the comparison target and risks a circular/ill-posed validation (comparing an observed correlation to another observation, not to theory). Cite a genuine linear-theory ISW prediction (e.g. from CAMB/CLASS with the same cosmology) as the reference.

With exactly 1000 realizations the minimum attainable rank-test p-value is ~0.001, and the ISW signal at nside=64 with photometric-redshift bins is expected to be weak (S/N ~1–3 in the literature). The spec should acknowledge the power floor: a null result cannot distinguish 'no signal' from 'under-powered', and the constitution-mandated N=1000 fixes this. At minimum SC-001/FR-010 should require reporting the expected signal-to-noise or the detectable effect size, not just the p-value.

'Monte-Carlo rank-test p-value for the observed correlation amplitude' — the scalar 'amplitude' is never defined (peak of ξ(θ)? integral over θ? per-bin?). FR-003 outputs a curve ξ(θ) but FR-004/SC-001 test a scalar; the reduction from curve to test statistic must be specified or the rank test is not well-defined.
